teaches.text: Techniques of memorization! The entire Vedas handed down orally through millenniums! Students learned forward sequence, backward, skipping syllables - remember it forever!

names.match: Avadhan. That's what this is called
names.text: Avadhan. That's what this is called. Many people ask questions. Expert has to remember all of them, then respond to each in verses following rules of rasa and alankara.

payoff.match: Professor explained their memorization technique to me
payoff.text: Professor explained their memorization technique to me. I tried it on a shloka and it worked.

verses.title: The pi shloka
verses.subtitle: gopī bhāgya madhuvrāta…
verses.source: Attributed to Jagadguru Swami Sri Bharati Krishna Tirthaji Maharaja, *Vedic Mathematics* — the verse quoted in the book's own notes.
verses.note: This is the one Dvij drills. Built as a mnemonic, so its surface sense is strained: it is carrying digits, not making an argument.

verses.title: One being, many names
verses.subtitle: ekaṃ sad viprā bahudhā vadanti
verses.source: Rigveda 1.164.46 — one of the oldest verses carried by exactly this method.
verses.note: "Truth is one; the wise call it by many names." The book reaches for the same idea when it wonders how the Rigveda's 33 gods became thirty-three *koti*.

distractions: SHHHH! The dignitaries turn and glare. How many of them?
A conch sounds. Brahmakaal has arrived. How many blasts?
The priest adds ghee to the fire. How many ladles?
